summary_for_children: Al-Qamar means The Moon. It tells of the moon splitting and of Nuh, 'Ad, Thamud, Lut and Pharaoh, and repeats that Allah made the Quran easy to remember.
world_title: Moon Split and the Easy Reminder
environment_concept: A full moon over the plain (54:1; the splitting itself is not pictured), pouring rain (54:11), springs bursting from the earth (54:12), a vessel of planks being built (54:13) and palms uprooted by the wind (54:20).
architecture_and_scenery: Night sky, a flood plain with a vessel of planks and nails, uprooted palms, a rocky valley with a she-camel's trail.

palette.lighting: Night with a pale moon, storm light

unique_world.visual_theme: A path through a quiet autumn valley at evening with four tall standing stones carved with lines

primary_mechanic.text: At each of four standing stones (Nuh, ‘Ad, Thamud, Lut), read the passage, then rebuild the refrain of 54:17 from its English pieces in order; two pieces are hidden at the first stone and all five at the last. Out-of-order pieces are refused.

secondary_activities: the Hour has come near (54:1, read; the moon is not pictured)
unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading at the start, four stones each with a story and the refrain, then a closing reading
world_assets: carved lines that light when remembered
environment_behaviour: a stone’s carved lines glow gold once its refrain is remembered
unique_world.learning_objective: Remember the refrain of 54:17 and the four peoples it follows

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Moon and the Warnings
story_library.children_narration: Surah Al-Qamar begins with the splitting of the moon as a sign, then recalls communities that rejected the messages sent to them. The stories of Nuh, 'Ad, Thamud, Lut's people, and Pharaoh's people remind us that guidance should not be ignored.

world_idea.title: The Moonlit History Atlas
world_idea.description: Explore a moonlit observatory connected to separate narrative environments. The opening sign is explained through scripture rather than presented as a scientifically reconstructed event.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The splitting of the moon (54:1) is not animated or reconstructed.
